elements.element: Customer has an express right to terminate for convenience on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other"; the right is expressed only as a bar to "automatically renewed" at "each anniversary", so a mid-term convenience right is not clearly conferred (official check: "Customer convenience termination present" = false)

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "equal to the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales ... divided by two, and (ii) the aggregate payments made by the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 in respect of the three (3) calendar months preceding the Termination Date"

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date, unless terminated by either Party" — HDI's right operates only at the anniversary/end of term

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term termination requires 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other"

elements.element: Customer may terminate on 30 days' written notice
Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer termination
elements.evidence: no refund language; only "the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice"

offending_extra_words: the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two, and (ii)
; provided, that no Termination Payment shall be due or payable if the Company terminates this Agreement pursuant to Section 1.6 or as a result of HDI's breach of this Agreement
reasons: The fee cap element of the fallback is achieved: the Termination Payment is now the lesser of the original formula and three months' Section 3.1 payments, and the 90-day mutual notice plus end-of-term-only structure fits the fallback notice and Vendor-side limits.

The fallback's Customer convenience-termination element is not demonstrably in place: the only termination mechanic is a non-renewal notice tied to "each anniversary of the Effective Date", so no mid-term Customer convenience right is conferred; the official check confirms this is absent and the redline did not add it.

Minimality fails: the operation rewrites the whole payment formula (34 words to 95, changed-character ratio 0.651), where a short cap insertion such as "but in no event more than three (3) months' fees" would suffice.

The added proviso excusing the Termination Payment where the Company terminates for HDI's breach or under Section 1.6 is a new exception beyond what the fallback cap requires, and duplicates protection already available on a breach termination.
